name: Sakarya Outwash Fan Apron
why_habitability: Distal apron of the Sakarya Vallis alluvial fan where ancient flood waters debouched onto the crater floor. Unconsolidated and cemented sediment sheets here preserve evidence of multiple episodic fluvial deposition events. Astronauts can examine grain sorting to assess peak discharge velocity.
notes: Distal outwash fan at the lower terminus of Sakarya Vallis.

name: Distal Channel Inflow Margin
why_habitability: A low-slope channel terminus cutting through the lower fan strata. This margin exposes fine-grained sedimentary layers deposited as flow slowed upon entering the open basin. Investigating these sediments may reveal evidence of lacustrine standing water or mudstones.
notes: Northern fan reach covered in HiRISE PSP_007501_1750.

name: Lower Alluvial Fan Splay
why_habitability: An expansive alluvial sediment splay displaying lateral gravel bars and low-relief channel bifurcations. Mineral-rich waters that flowed through this fan likely precipitated sulfates and clays during drying phases. Sampling this flat outcrop offers high potential for detecting preserved geochemical biosignatures.
notes: Alluvial debris deposits and sulfate-cemented sedimentary units.

name: Stratified Footwall Terrace
why_habitability: A gently sloping terrace flanking the eastern canyon mouth exposing intact stratified sulfate bedrock. These rhythmic strata record fluctuating groundwater levels and lake highstands prior to canyon incision. It provides safe ground access to measure primary bedding thickness without ascending steep cliffs.
notes: Stratified canyon wall base documented in HiRISE observation.

name: Canyon Mouth Floor Gateway
why_habitability: The flat, walkable entrance floor of Sakarya Vallis where down-canyon debris flows transition into the lower fan. The deposit contains a heterogeneous mixture of boulders and cemented matrix transported from Mount Sharp's interior. This allows comprehensive sampling of upper stratigraphy directly from walkable ground.
notes: Debris flows and groundwater exfiltration at the lower canyon mouth.
